question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool scheduler in the core agent loop, and what safety and ordering contract must gate it?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix changes core runtime semantics and safety policy rather than repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for streaming scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

options.title: Wait For Tool Safety Metadata
options.body: Defer implementation until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract gives the scheduler a reliable policy input.

options.title: Keep Batch-After-Stream
options.body: Decide that current post-stream parallel batching remains the only supported core behavior because early execution is too risky for the default runtime.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for streaming scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent runtime extraction and tool-call handling work spans the central agent-core and provider stream surfaces that this design would need to preserve.
